9dcb3cf
slice 5.7: BDEV band + `memory` ramdisk driver + `tools/mkfs-mfs` + rootfs blob

Builds the bottom two layers of the storage stack Phase 5's milestone needs
(D3): a MinixFS v3 image built at compile time, packed into the MXBI archive as
a non-ELF blob, copied into RAM frames and mapped into the `memory` driver's
address space at boot, and served over a new BDEV request band. Slice 5.8 puts
MFS on top of it; 5.9 closes the milestone.

ABI. `BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00`, between VFS (`0x800`) and CDEV (`0xB00`), leaving
`0x900` for 5.8's VFS<->FS band — four in-tree comments recorded that pairing
the other way round and are corrected here; only ascending order is
load-bearing. Payload mirrors CDEV: `{minor, grant, len, block}`, with **no
granter field** (the driver takes it from the kernel-stamped `m_source`, the
5.2/5.3 confused-deputy rule) and **no grant-offset field** (every client
through 5.9 grants a buffer whose block starts at 0). Reply `m_type` is the
byte count.

Two deliberate departures from CDEV. An over-long or out-of-range request is
`EINVAL`, not a short read: a short *write* is a POSIX contract clients loop
over, but a filesystem cannot interpret half a block, and `EIO` stays reserved
for Phase 6's real media errors. And `BDEV_WRITE` is defined now and answers
`EROFS`, not `ENOSYS` — `ENOSYS` is already the unknown-`m_type` answer, so
reusing it would make "doesn't know about writes" and "knows and refuses"
indistinguishable. It validates before refusing, so 5.10 replaces one line.

Kernel. `uspace::RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE = 0x8000_0000` (one L1 slot, 4 MiB) sits
*above* the device window on purpose: `region::REGION_LIMIT` is the base of the
lowest kernel-owned window, so VM needs no edit when a window is added. The
pre-map is a `nr == MEM_PROC_NR` arm in `load_boot_server` beside TTY's — not in
`load_exec_image`, which `do_exec` shares — with no TLB or cache maintenance
(both justified in situ) and no `prot.device` involvement, since these are
ordinary RAM frames. Every step `.expect()`s: a non-advancing loop must panic on
`AlreadyMapped`, not leave a 1-page ramdisk and 255 leaked frames. New

## Commits

- **Every commit must carry a DCO sign-off** — always `git commit --signoff` (`-s`), which appends
  `Signed-off-by: Kevin Barnard <kevin.barnard@gmail.com>` from `user.name`/`user.email`. It is the
  Developer Certificate of Origin attestation, not a stylistic trailer: it asserts the author has
  the right to contribute the code under BSD-3-Clause. Never hand-write the trailer for someone
  else, and never add one on their behalf — `--signoff` signs off *as the committer*, which is the
  whole point. Every non-merge commit in this repo's history has one; keep it that way
- Sign-off is **orthogonal to GPG signing** — `--signoff` is the DCO trailer, `--gpg-sign` (on by
  default here) is the cryptographic signature. Both are required, and neither substitutes for the
  other. The global rules still hold: never `--no-gpg-sign`, never `--no-verify`
- Trailer order in the message footer is `Co-Authored-By:` → `Entire-Checkpoint:` → `Signed-off-by:`
  (git appends the sign-off last). Amending or rebasing drops nothing, but `git commit --amend`
  without `-s` on a commit you re-author still needs the trailer present — check with
  `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Signed-off-by)'` before pushing
- Merge commits created by GitHub's UI have **no** sign-off; that is expected and not worth fixing.
  Only the authored commits inside a PR need one

Added a `## Commits` section to `/Users/kevinbarnard/src/minixrs/CLAUDE.md:160`, between `## CI` and `## Architecture`:

- **DCO sign-off is mandatory** — always `git commit --signoff`, and it's framed as the Developer Certificate of Origin attestation (right to contribute under BSD-3-Clause), not a stylistic trailer. Includes the rule that `--signoff` signs off *as the committer*, so never hand-write the trailer for someone else.
- **Sign-off is orthogonal to GPG signing** — `--signoff` is the DCO trailer, `--gpg-sign` is the crypto signature; both required, neither substitutes for the other. Cross-references the existing global never-`--no-gpg-sign`/`--no-verify` rules.
- **Trailer order** (`Co-Authored-By:` → `Entire-Checkpoint:` → `Signed-off-by:`) matching what's actually in the history, plus the `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Signed-off-by)'` pre-push check for the `--amend`-without-`-s` case.
- **GitHub merge commits have no sign-off** and that's expected — only authored commits inside a PR need one.

Verified before writing it: all 102 non-merge commits in the repo already carry `Signed-off-by: Kevin Barnard <kevin.barnard@gmail.com>`, so the "keep it that way" claim is factual.

Two things I did **not** do, since you asked only for the CLAUDE.md note:

1. **Placement** — I put it in the project CLAUDE.md rather than your global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (where `## Commit Signing` lives), because DCO is a per-project contribution policy and a global rule would add trailers in repos whose maintainers don't use DCO. Say the word if you'd rather it be global, or in both.
2. **No CI enforcement** — there's no DCO check in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so this is convention-only. I can add a DCO gate (GitHub's DCO app, or a `git log` check job) if you want it enforced rather than remembered.
